input.task: Review six commits against the factory's own CODING_STANDARDS.md and its smell baseline. The commits add a scenario-table core document and wire it into to-spec, the architect runner prompt and the poteto-mode playbooks, through patches and the template copies. Sort every finding into the four required headings.
input.done: A Markdown report exists at .scratch/review/ab47eb9/standards-report.md. It has exactly four `## ` headings, in this order: Would break, Fails open, Standards breaches, Fix alongside. Items are numbered continuously across all four headings, and each opens with a bold title and quotes its hunk in a fenced block. Every Would break and Fails open item also has a `Documented step:` line and a `Result:` line. The report ends with a single `hard findings: N` line, where N counts only the items under the first two headings. My reply is nothing but that file path.
input.may_change: I can read any file in the repo, including the 572-line diff at .scratch/review/ab47eb9/diff, and run read-only commands such as grep, git log/show/diff, the test scripts and check_knowledge.py. The only file I may create is the report itself.
input.must_not: I must not edit, fix or commit anything in the repo. That covers the generated files (docs/knowledge/spec, pages, notes, template/docs/factory918), research/ and the vendored skills. I must not push, comment on a PR or ticket, or run anything that writes to the tree. I must not report anything the CI gate already enforces, and I must not treat an unsupported edge case that fails with a correctable error as a finding. Everything outside the report goes in no reply text.
unsettled: What counts as the 'documented path' for a change that is almost all prose and patches, and so what can honestly go under Would break or Fails open. The brief names no ticket or spec to quote in the Documented step line.

How to check that the generated files (template/docs/factory918/*, the INDEX) match their sources without running build_knowledge.py or sync, since both write to the tree. Options are to diff by hand, to run them in a throwaway copy, or to skip the check.

How to confirm that the hand edits to the vendored skill files under template/.agents/skills match the new and changed patches in patches/ and series. The same question applies to whether SOURCES.md describes them.
Which rules the CI gate already enforces and should therefore be skipped. Answering this means reading .github/workflows/factory-ci.yml.

How to judge the count claims, for example 'six core documents' in AGENTS.md now that a sixth file was added. Is that a Standards breach under the rule that counts must be true at the commit, or only a judgement call?
How hard to apply code smells like Shotgun Surgery or Duplicated Code to a change that touches 29 files and duplicates text between the patches and the template by design.
questions: Is there a ticket or spec for this change whose lines I should quote as the Documented step? If not, which file:line should a would-break finding cite?

What base commit should I diff against: the parent of 3b48036, or something else such as main?
Should the deliberate duplication between patches/ and template/.agents/skills be left out of the smell findings?
